title: Big Data with Hadoop — Palmer Penguins

slides.title: Penguins on Hadoop
slides.subtitle: HDFS, Hive, WebHDFS ELT and PySpark on one dataset

slides.title: HDFS
slides.body: Create the folder, download, put, list.

slides.title: Data lands in HDFS
slides.body: penguins.csv copied into /user/maria_dev/datasets and verified healthy.
slides.notes: Commands: hdfs dfs -mkdir -p, curl download, hdfs dfs -put -f, hdfs dfs -ls. fsck shows 1 block, HEALTHY.

slides.title: Hive
slides.body: penguins_db.penguins_raw with NA mapped to NULL.

slides.title: HiveQL results
slides.notes: Gentoo 124 on Biscoe, Chinstrap 68 on Dream, Adelie on all three islands. Gentoo average 5076 g, 217 mm.

slides.title: Missing values
slides.notes: From Hive query 3c using SUM(CASE WHEN ... IS NULL).

slides.title: ELT
slides.body: Jupyter reads HDFS through WebHDFS InsecureClient.

items.heading: Drop
items.body: 2 rows with no measurements removed (344 to 342)

items.heading: Impute
items.body: Numeric gaps filled with species median

items.heading: Convert
items.body: body_mass_kg added, file uploaded to datasets/clean in HDFS

slides.title: Clean data back in HDFS
slides.body: Notebook uploads the cleaned file and reads it back to verify.

slides.title: PySpark
slides.body: spark-submit reads, filters, sorts, caches and writes JSON.

slides.title: Spark job output
slides.body: Schema printed, 177 heavy penguins kept, cached and saved partitioned by species.

slides.title: Partitioned JSON
slides.body: species=Adelie, Chinstrap and Gentoo folders under spark/output/penguins.

slides.title: What the data says
slides.body: Gentoo are the heaviest at 5.08 kg with 217 mm flippers.

slides.title: Pipeline runs end to end
slides.body: Every stage reads from and writes back to HDFS, so each step can be re-run alone.
